instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-1003 Minimum Wage Act Revision Act - requirements (minimum wage, coverage, overtime, tipped wage)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage indexed each July 1 by prior-year annual average CPI-U Washington MSA, rounded to nearest 0.05 (a)(6); amount published by DOES at least 30 days before (f-1). Coverage: employee regularly >50% of working time in DC, or based in DC with substantial DC time and not >50% in any one state (b); DC minimum for each DC hour if >=2 hours of DC work in a workweek (b-1). Overtime 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/workweek (c); retail/service commission exemption (e). Tipped minimum: 10.00 from 2024-07-01 (f)(5); 56% of minimum wage from 2026-07-01 (f)(6A); 60% 2028-07-01; 65% 2030-07-01; 70% 2032-07-01; 75% 2034-07-01 (as amended by D.C. Law 26-55 sec. 2222(a), eff. 2025-12-06, applying as of 2025-07-25). DC government and DC-contract employees excluded from the tipped schedule (i). Office-building security officers: SCA Guard 1 wage+fringe (h).

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-1302 When wages must be paid
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Regular paydays designated in advance, at least twice per calendar month; bona fide administrative, executive, professional employees at least monthly; not more than 10 working days between end of pay period and payday. Same rule as US-DC-P5-1-013, now with local file.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-1303 Payment of wages upon discharge or resignation
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Unless a CBA provides otherwise: discharge = wages paid not later than the working day following discharge (4 days if employee handled employer monies); resignation (no written contract >30 days) = next regular payday or within 7 days, whichever earlier; labor-dispute suspension = next regular payday. Liquidated damages 10% of unpaid wages per working day or treble wages, whichever smaller.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-531.02 Accrued Sick and Safe Leave Act - provision of paid leave
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: 100+ employees: 1 h per 37 h worked, cap 7 days/calendar year; 25-99: 1 h per 43 h, cap 5 days; 24 or fewer: 1 h per 87 h, cap 3 days; size = average monthly FTE of prior calendar year; FLSA-exempt accrue on max 40 h/week. Accrual from start of employment per pay period, use after 90 days; reinstated on rehire within 1 year. Tipped restaurant/bar employees: 1 h per 43 h, cap 5 days, paid at full DC minimum wage (g). Salon commission rate formula (f).

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-531.01 Accrued Sick and Safe Leave Act - definitions
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee excludes: unpaid volunteers of nonprofit/religious organizations, lay religious officers, casual babysitters, independent contractors, students, health-care workers in a premium-pay program, DCPS substitute teachers/aides for 30 or fewer consecutive days. Employer includes the District government. No work-location (percentage-of-time) test is stated in this definition.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 16-572 Attachment of wages; percentage limitations; priority
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Creditor wage attachment limited to 25% of the amount by which weekly disposable wages exceed 40 x DC minimum hourly wage (CCPA uses 30 x federal minimum; DC protects more); other pay periods per Mayor regulation; continuing levy; only one attachment satisfied at a time, the first delivered to the marshal has priority.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-541.01 Universal Paid Leave - definitions (covered employee, wages)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Covered employee: spends >50% of work time for the employer in DC, or employment based in DC with substantial DC work time and not >50% in another jurisdiction. Wages = UI wages under 51-101(3) (no PFL wage cap stated). Multistate answer: PFL tax follows this test, not residence.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 51-101 Unemployment compensation - definitions (employment localization, wages)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Standard UI localization test: service localized in DC, or not localized anywhere and base of operations/direction and control in DC, or residence in DC; reciprocal election arrangements under 51-116. Wages = all remuneration incl. commissions, bonuses, non-cash value and customary tips; excludes employer retirement/sickness/medical/death plan payments and employer-paid FICA.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 2-220.03 Living Wage Act - living wage payment
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Recipients of DC contracts or government assistance of 100,000 USD or more pay affiliated employees the living wage; subcontractors from 15,000 (contract) / 50,000 (assistance). DOES adjusts each January 1 by CPI-U Washington MSA up to 3%, nearest 0.05, published by March 1; never below the DC minimum wage (f).

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-1008 Wage statement and notice (re-read with local file)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: See findings DC.md section 4 (content of statement, notice at hire, record retention).

instrument_name: DOES Office of Wage and Hour Public Notice - District of Columbia Minimum Wage Increase (2026)
authority: DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Wage and Hour
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage 17.95 USD/h (2025-07-01 to 2026-06-30) -> 18.40 USD/h from 2026-07-01, all employers regardless of size; CPI (Washington MSA) increase 2025 = 2.4%. Tipped base wage 10.00 -> 10.30 from 2026-07-01, employer pays any shortfall to the full minimum (weekly average). Derivation: 17.95 x 1.024 = 18.3808 -> nearest 0.05 = 18.40 (32-1003(a)(6)); 56% x 18.40 = 10.304 -> 10.30 (32-1003(f)(6A)).

instrument_name: DOES Notice of Living Wage Increase to Employers (2026)
authority: DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Wage-Hour
figure_or_rule_carried: Living wage (DC contractors and assistance recipients of 100,000+) 17.95 USD/h from 2026-01-01 to 2026-06-30; 18.40 USD/h from 2026-07-01 (floor = minimum wage, 2-220.03(f)).

instrument_name: OTR Withholding Tax Forms page (live copy 2026-11-02)
authority: DC Office of Tax and Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: Live page (plain curl, 200) restates US-DC-P5-1-003: 2026 FR-900Q filed electronically on MyTax.DC.gov; deposits by the 20th after the period, filing by the last day of the month after the quarter; FR-900A for annual filers below 200 USD/year (2026 return due 2027-01-31, deposit 2027-01-20); FR-900NP for 1099/W-2G withholding; Form WT paper W-2/1099 transmittal due January 31; household employers report withholding on FR-900Q with an FEIN since 2019; D-4 and D-4A both marked 'currently under review' (no fill-in link on the page).

instrument_name: OTR 2026 FR-900Q Employer/Payor Withholding Tax Reporting Instructions (Rev. 09/2025)
authority: DC Office of Tax and Revenue
article_or_section: General Instructions; When must you file; Specific Instructions
figure_or_rule_carried: Every employer paying wages to a DC resident withholds and files FR-900Q (or FR-900A per assigned frequency); quarterly filers file even with zero tax. Payments weekly, semi-weekly, monthly or quarterly as assigned by OTR, by the 20th of the month after the period; return due Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31. Electronic filing mandatory since TY2023 on MyTax.DC.gov; FEIN required; payments over 5,000 USD per period must be electronic; ACH credit tax type code 00300, period YYMMDD; no IAT; dishonored payment fee 65 USD; amended return = another FR-900Q flagged amended; final return flag on cessation. Registration via FR-500 on MyTax.DC.gov (no auto-registration).

instrument_name: OTR 2025 MyTax.DC.gov W-2/W-2C (EFW2/EFW2C) Electronic Filing Instructions v1.0
authority: DC Office of Tax and Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: DC accepts the SSA EFW2/EFW2C file with a REQUIRED RS (state wage) record; RO/RU/RV optional and not relevant to DC; RE employment code optional. Electronic filing mandatory at 25 or more W-2/W-2C via MyTax.DC.gov (bulk upload or third-party multi-employer); fewer than 25 may file paper with Form WT or online manual entry (up to 24). Deadline January 31 each year. Edition is tax year 2025 (filed January 2026); a 2026 edition (for filing January 2027) was not found at the analogous URL (404).

instrument_name: DOES Employer Self Service Portal landing page (live copy 2026-11-02)
authority: DC Department of Employment Services
figure_or_rule_carried: For calendar year 2026 Tax Table VI remains in effect for experience-rated employers (51-103(c)(3),(c)(4)(B),(c)(8)(A)); new employer rate 2.7%; administrative assessment fee 0.2%; taxable wage base 9,000.00 USD unchanged. 2026 rate notices for quarterly filers mailed 2026-01-30; household annual filers' rates mailed in 2026/Q3. 2026/Q3 wage report and payment due 2026-10-31 (51-104(b),(c)); annual (household) filers' 2025 report due 2026-04-15. Late interest 1.5% per month. Same content as US-DC-P5-1-008, now with local file.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 51-103 Unemployment compensation contributions (rate tables, wage base, surcharge, assessment)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Table VI (used when the Fund is not above 0.8% of payrolls): 1.9% (reserve >= 8.0%) up to 4.4% (reserve 0.0-1.5%), then 6.2%, 6.5%, 6.8%, 7.1%, 7.4% (reserve <= -10.0%); 2026 range therefore 1.9%-7.4% plus 0.2% admin assessment (and 0.1% interest surcharge (l)(1) where billed). Wage base: wages exclude any amount above 9,000 USD actually paid to any person in a calendar year (e)(6); the subsection states no rule crediting wages reported to another state. Contributions may not be deducted from wages (d).

instrument_name: D.C. Code 51-104 Payment of employer contributions (quarterly return, household annual option, electronic filing, penalties)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI return and payment by the last day of the month after the quarter; household employers may file and pay annually on April 15; employers with 250+ employees in a quarter must file wage reports by machine-readable method approved by the Director; interest 1.5% per month; penalty 10% (minimum 100 USD) if not paid/filed by the first day of the second month after the quarter; fractions of a cent below 0.5 disregarded, 0.5 or more rounded up to 0.01 (g).

instrument_name: DC Paid Family Leave tax calculators page with historical rate table (live copy 2026-11-02)
authority: DC DOES Office of Paid Family Leave
article_or_section: Tax due dates; Historical PFL Tax Rate Information
figure_or_rule_carried: PFL employer tax 0.75% for all four quarters of 2026 (also 2024-Q3 to 2025-Q4); history 0.62% 2019-Q2 to 2022-Q2, 0.26% 2022-Q3 to 2024-Q2. Wage report and tax due Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31 via ESSP; opted-in self-employed use ESSP or form PFL-30S. 100% employer-funded.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 32-541.03 Contributions to the Universal Paid Leave Fund (as amended by D.C. Act 26-416)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Covered employer contributes 0.75% of wages of each covered employee (a); opted-in self-employed 0.75% of income (b); collections above the CFO-certified solvency need go to the General Fund (b-1, wording amended by D.C. Act 26-416 sec. 4052(a), 2026-08-13: rate unchanged); non-payment follows 51-104 interest and penalties (f). Statute states no wage cap.

instrument_name: D.C. Act 26-416 Fiscal Year 2027 Budget Support Emergency Act of 2026 (73 DCR 11509)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
article_or_section: Title IV Subtitle F secs. 4051-4053 (Universal Paid Leave); Title VII Subtitle I secs. 7111-7113 (Tax Code Conformity and Clarification); sec. 9001, 9003
figure_or_rule_carried: STATUS: emergency act, effective 2026-08-13 on Mayor approval, in force for no longer than 90 days (sec. 9003); general applicability 2026-10-01 (sec. 9001). The permanent FY2027 Budget Support Act passed the Council second vote on 2026-07-07 (secondary lead only); its D.C. Law number and congressional-review completion were not read. LEVEL: (1) assessment only: DC basic standard deduction decoupled from federal for TY2025-2029 = 15,000 single/MFS, 22,500 HoH, 30,000 joint (2025), COLA from 2026 rounded down to 50 (47-1801.04(3A)); personal exemptions 47-1806.02 repealed; federal qualified-tips (IRC 224), qualified-overtime (IRC 225), car-loan interest and enhanced senior deductions disallowed for TY2025 but allowed as DC deductions for TY beginning after 2025-12-31 (new 47-1803.04); DC EITC 85% of federal for TY2026-2028; subtitle applies as of 2025-01-01 (sec. 7113). (2) PFL benefit side: maximum weekly benefit 1,100 USD from 2026-10-01, CPI-indexed thereafter; max durations for claims 2026-10-01 to 2030-09-30: parental 12, family 6, medical 10, pre-natal 2 workweeks. No change found to withholding statute 47-1812.08, PFL rate 0.75%, UI, or minimum wage.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 46-226.06 Directory of New Hires
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Within 20 days of the date an employee begins employment in DC or is rehired, report: employee name, address, SSN; employer name, address, FEIN; date of hire (first day of services for compensation). Optional: contact name/phone, medical insurance availability and eligibility date, date of birth, compensation. On W-4 or equivalent form, by first-class mail, magnetically or electronically; electronic reporters may send 2 monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate electronic reporters may designate one state with written notice to HHS; penalty 25 USD per employee (500 USD for conspiracy), per month until compliance.

instrument_name: DC Office of the Attorney General, Child Support Services Division - New Hire Reporting page
authority: Office of the Attorney General for the District of Columbia (IV-D agency)
figure_or_rule_carried: Channel: District of Columbia Directory of New Hires operated by a contractor at https://dc-newhire.com/ (online after registration with FEIN and email; mail to PO Box 457 Norwell MA 02061 (page also shows PO Box 366 Holbrook MA 02343); fax (877) 892-6388); file-transfer section for payroll-software exports. 20-day rule restated.

instrument_name: DOES Accrued Sick and Safe Leave Act Fact Sheet
authority: DC Department of Employment Services, Office of Wage-Hour
figure_or_rule_carried: Coverage: workers who spend at least 50% of their time working in DC (fact sheet wording; the statute definition 32-531.01 states no location test, the threshold sits in the regulations 7 DCMR 3200-3299, not read). Accrued leave carries over year to year; no cash payout of unused paid sick leave required on resignation or termination; use capped at the annual accrual maximum; certification may be required after 3+ consecutive days; time and payroll records showing leave use kept at least 3 years. Not covered: students, health-care premium-pay participants, unpaid volunteers, lay religious officers, construction-industry employees under a bona fide CBA. Same accrual tiers as 32-531.02.

instrument_name: D.C. Code 47-1812.08 Withholding of tax (local copy 2026-11-02)
authority: Council of the District of Columbia
figure_or_rule_carried: Restates US-DC-P5-1-001 / US-DCR3-001 with a local file: employer elects percentage method or tables similar in principle to IRC 3402, or another method by regulation (b)(1); no standard-deduction allowance in withholding (b)(1A); wages may be computed to the nearest dollar (b)(2)(C); no flat supplemental rate in the section; resident lump-sum retirement distributions withheld at the highest DC rate (m); annual employee statement (g) and CFO statements (n). Section history lists emergency D.C. Act 26-214 (2025-12-03) touching (m) only. D.C. Act 26-416 (2026-08-13) did not amend this section but repealed personal exemptions (47-1806.02), which removes the basis of D-4 withholding allowances (OTR marks D-4 'under review', US-DCS5-013).
